tracks.narration: Two threads, one shared resource — and only one of them can have it at a time.
Test and set is one hardware instruction that does two things at once. It reads the lock's old value and writes one — atomically, so no other thread can slip in between.
Two threads race for the lock. Thread one calls test and set first, gets back zero, and walks in. Thread two calls a moment later, gets back one, and has to wait.
Thread two keeps trying. Each loop reads one, sees the lock is taken, and spins. When thread one finishes its work and writes zero, the very next call returns zero — and now thread two is the holder.
Spin while busy. One atomic step does the test and the set together — and that is the simplest lock in computing.
